content.introduction: This week's economic calendar features key data releases, including the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCE) and Core PCE on Wednesday, September 30, and the September jobs report. The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and the PCE data are expected to show the impact of rising interest rates and economic conditions. Additionally, Consumer Spending and PCE Price Index data for August will be released on Thursday. The sources also mention the S&P Case-Shiller Home Price Index and the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index, both on Tuesday, September 29. The Job Openings & Labor Turnover Survey is also scheduled for release on the same day.
body:
There is no shortage of incoming data as the economic calendar turns to October this week. With interest rates on the rise, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and the September jobs report are on tap.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) will release Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCE) data for August before the opening bell on Thursday. [...] Wednesday, September 30: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index (PCE) and Core PCE: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) re-heated in August along with re-escalating war in the Middle East and rising energy prices at home. Is it unreasonable to expect a similar trajectory for PCE? [...] "We expect the FOMC to remain mindful of inconsistencies between the payroll and household surveys," Giannoni writes, "where we expect another flat reading for the unemployment rate (at 4.1%) amid low labor supply growth."

The economist says this combination "would keep an FOMC hold in play for the October meeting, as it continues to assess data developments," but he also expects another 25-basis-point rate hike in December.

Reporting schedules are provided Forex Factory and MarketWatch.

Management upped its full-year revenue guidance to $1.04 billion and $1.05 billion from $990 million to $1 billion, above a consensus estimate of $1 billion. Earnings will fall between $6.15 and $6.23 per share, in line with analysts' forecast.

It is enough to help the AI software maker emerge from under the radar and survive the SaaSmageddon? [...] That's a tough lead-up to management's report on fiscal 2027 first-quarter results after the closing bell on Thursday. Wall Street expects a 10.2% year-over-year slide for EPS to 44 cents, on a 3.3% decline for revenue.

The consumer discretionary stock was down almost 42% year to date and more than 77% from its November 5, 2021, all-time high through September 24. Its market cap has fallen from a peak of about $281 billion to $53.5 billion. [...] Progress Software (PRGS) logo displayed on a smartphone screen.

Progress Software (PRGS) logo displayed on a smartphone screen.

Progress Software (PRGS) reported fiscal third quarter earnings of $1.69 per share on revenue of $246 million. Wall Street expected the small-cap stock to report EPS of $1.52 on revenue of $247 million.
